newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila cautions against wage hike, cites inflation.
newsitem.headline: Manila cautions against wage hike, cites inflation.

text.p: The government's National Economic Development Authority warned on Wednesday inflation would go back to double-digit levels if daily wages are increased by 45 pesos as demanded by labour unions.

In a paper presented to the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council, Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said "the proposed 45 pesos per day wage hike will result in double digit average inflation for 1996 of 10 to 11 percent."
Habito said inflation could quicken to 14.7 to 19.6 percent in November and 15.2 to 20.2 percent in December on a year-on-year basis.
Inflation was 4.7 percent in October. It was at double-digit levels since September 1995 due to rice supply shortages before tapering to a single-digit level in June 1996.

If there are no wage increases and price adjustments are made to cover for oil, power and transport hike fares, he said inflation will remain single-digit, resulting in a full-year average of 8.5 to 8.7 percent.
The November inflation is estimated to reach 6.0 to 6.3 percent, and December, 6.5 to 6.8 percent, he said.

Labour unions had petitioned for an increase in wages to help workers cope with the rising prices of consumer goods due to the increase in oil prices. The 45-peso increase would result in a daily minimum wage of 142 pesos.
Starting in August, the government adopted an automatic oil pricing mechanism which would pave the way for the full deregulation of the oil industry by March 1997.
The new scheme allowed the government to change prices of petroleum products monthly based on Singapore posted prices.
